node.label: Jay Winter
node.date_label: Sites of Memory, Sites of Mourning (1995) · Remembering War (2006) · War Beyond Words (2017)
node.description: A historian of modern war and remembrance who examines the mediation of suffering through museums, images, language and silence. His account of public history treats memory as a right while refusing to promise that remembrance necessarily heals.

proposed_edges.relationship: Examines how art, museums and silence mediate remembrance of modern war.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own interview treats memory through changing forms of representation; remembrance is not equated with accurate or therapeutic recovery.

proposed_edges.relationship: Contributes to the Historial museum’s international research and display of the Great War.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own museum answers explain proposing a research centre and a wider war history, with many collaborators; he is not credited as sole creator.
